title: What If We Could Make Clouds Drop Snow? Scientists Tried

scenes.text: What if we could make clouds drop snow on demand? Scientists have been trying for decades.
The trick is silver iodide, released into cold clouds so ice crystals form around it.
In Idaho in 2017, one seeding flight made snow for about 67 minutes over roughly 900 square miles.
Radar and snow gauges confirmed it, but the extra layer was only about a tenth of a millimeter.
A six-winter Wyoming test found no statistically significant gain, though modeling hinted at 5 to 15 percent more streamflow.
So it works, but only in clouds that already exist. Nobody can make a cloud from clear sky.
